div.head: VI As 6.2
div.ab: ⁊ oxan to mancuse ⁊ cú to XX ⁊ swyn to X ⁊ sceap to scll'.
Et bos una manca (id est XXX den.) et uacca XX den. et porcus X den. et ouis solido (V den.) persoluatur.
⁊ oxan to mancuse ⁊ cú to XX ⁊ swyn to X ⁊ sceap to scll.
Und einen Ochsen [ersetzen wir dem Genossen taxirt] zu 1 Mancus und eine Kuh zu 20 (Pfennig Quadr.) und ein Schwein zu 10 (Pfennig Quadr.) und ein Schaf zu 1 Schilling.
And an ox [we replace to the fellow-member, valued] at 1 mancus, and a cow at 20 (pence, Quadr.), and a pig at 10 (pence, Quadr.), and a sheep at 1 shilling.
An ox shall be valued at a mancus, and a cow at twenty pence, a pig at ten pence, and a sheep at a shilling.
An an ox [is to be paid for] at a mancus; and a cow at 20 [pence]; and a pig at 10 [pence]; and a sheep at a shilling.

Q missversteht den Schilling Westsächsisch, während das Orig. den Mercischen meint; s. o. 2¹
Q misunderstands the shilling as West Saxon, whereas the orig. means the Mercian; see above 2¹
Cf. Duns. cap. 7, which among other valuations gives that of the horse to be 30 shillings; the ox, 30 pence; the cow, 24 pence; the pig, 8 pence; and the sheep, a shilling.
Quadr. inserts id est xxx den. after una manca, and v den. after ouis solido. This is the value of the West Saxon shilling (see note 1, cap. 2, above). For mancus see note 2 to A. and G. cap. 3.
